root_cause: The mirroring/reflection logic used to clamp filter indices near image boundaries was implemented as a single conditional reflection (`ii < 0 ? -ii : ...`) rather than a proper repeated/folded mirroring, which is only valid when the amount of overshoot does not exceed the array dimension itself. Small image dimensions (smaller than filt_w/2) violate this assumption, allowing indices computed as `i - filt_w/2 + filt_i` to overshoot by more than h or w, producing indices still out of the valid [0, dim-1] range after one reflection.
findings: In vif_filter1d(), when computing the vertical and horizontal 1D filter passes near image edges, out-of-range indices ii/jj are 'mirrored' back into range using a single-step reflection: `ii = ii < 0 ? -ii : (ii >= h ? 2*h - ii - 1 : ii)` (and analogously for jj/w). This single reflection only corrects an index that is out of range by up to h (or w) once. Because the filter half-width is filt_w/2
